29 — GEO and AEO Checklist#

Improve how clearly and reliably a project can be understood, sourced, and answered by search answer systems and generative AI. GEO = Generative Engine Optimization; AEO = Answer Engine Optimization. Neither guarantees citation or inclusion.

Scope: Backend / API-specific. This file is one part of the 29_GEO_and_AEO.md checklist. Apply the domain-wide release gate across all applicable scope files; each checklist ID remains unique.

Review details#

  • Project / product:
  • Release / version / environment:
  • Scope and applicable jurisdictions / markets:
  • Reviewer / owner:
  • Review date:
  • Decision: Pending / Approved / Approved with documented exceptions / Blocked

How to use#

  1. Copy this template into each project's review records; keep the shared repository template unchecked.
  2. Check [x] only after verifying the item with evidence. For any inapplicable item, record N/A and the reason in the project's own review notes or issue tracker using its checklist ID; do not mark it as passed.
  3. Record evidence links or artifact references by checklist ID. Open an issue for every failed item, assign an owner and due date, and retest after remediation.
  4. Apply the release gate below. These checklists guide review; they do not replace qualified specialist review when required.

Machine readability and discovery#

  • GEO-023 Server responses, access controls, and bot rules are intentionally configured for the target discovery channels.

Measurement and iteration#

  • GEO-054 Recheck content accuracy after changes to source APIs, catalog feeds, and structured data.
  • GEO-081 For owned sites where AI-search access monitoring is relevant and authorized, review edge/CDN/origin request logs for provider-documented search crawlers and user-initiated fetchers as separate classes. Verify bot identity using current provider IP ranges or verified-bot signals where available (treat user-agent text alone as untrusted); group permitted public-page requests by canonical URL, time window, response status and block/challenge reason, including 3xx/403/429/5xx and missing log coverage. Investigate missing or failed visits against robots, WAF/CDN, authentication, internal links and delivered HTML without treating raw request counts, zero log rows, training bots or user-agent matches as proof of search indexing, AI citations, rankings or demand. Redact sensitive paths/query data and restrict/retain logs according to privacy and security policy.

API Checks#

Apply to API endpoints, client integrations, webhooks, or data feeds present in the project. Record N/A with reasons if none exist.

Reference basis: Google Search Central — AI features and your website; Google Search Central — Guide to optimizing for generative AI features; Google Search Central — JavaScript SEO basics.

  • GEO-055 Identify authoritative public APIs or feeds that supply facts displayed on answer-oriented pages and their update frequency.
  • GEO-056 Verify API-backed claims, entities, units, dates, product versions, and prices match the canonical human-readable pages.
  • GEO-057 Publish accurate, maintainable API reference or OpenAPI documentation when developer discovery is an actual use case.
  • GEO-058 Ensure public API documentation includes purpose, limits, examples, versioning, and the date of last substantive update.
  • GEO-059 Keep canonical pages available as accessible HTML; do not presume raw JSON API responses are indexed or cited as search pages.
  • GEO-060 Handle stale cache, failed API calls, and missing records so the site never silently presents inaccurate answer facts.
  • GEO-061 Verify schema/data feed identifiers match the intended organization, product, and page URLs.
  • GEO-062 Check licensing, provenance, and permitted public reuse before exposing datasets or AI-oriented machine-readable feeds.
  • GEO-063 Use structured API error statuses and document fallback behavior for consumers when the source data is unavailable.
  • GEO-064 Record change ownership for API schemas and upstream data fields that drive answer summaries and public claims.
  • GEO-065 Use access controls for non-public API data; do not publish private facts merely to improve AI discovery.

Release gate#

  • All applicable high-priority checks above pass, or an authorized decision-maker has explicitly accepted and documented each residual risk.
  • Failed items have tracked remediation, owners, and deadlines; material blockers remain blocked until resolved.
  • Evidence links and the reviewer, review date, and final decision are recorded.

Domain-specific approval rule: Do not approve deceptive, fabricated, or unsubstantiated content. Verify essential public facts and make evidence available; AI answer visibility cannot be promised.

Trusted references and scope#

The checks above are adapted into practical verification questions from these authoritative publications (not copied as standards text). Verify current versions and the project's scope before sign-off.

  • Google Search Central — AI features and your website
  • Google Search Central — Guide to optimizing for generative AI features
  • Google Search Central — JavaScript SEO basics
  • Google Search Central — Structured data introduction
  • OpenAI — Overview of OpenAI crawlers — search versus training versus user-action bots and provider IP ranges.
  • Anthropic — Crawler access guidance — Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User roles; published IP verification may be unavailable.
  • Perplexity — Crawler guidance — PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User distinction, bot IP sources.
  • OpenAPI Specification 3.2.1
  • NIST — Generative AI Risk Management Profile

GEO/AEO techniques are not separate eligibility requirements for Google AI Overviews or AI Mode. Google documents ordinary Search eligibility, helpful content, and no required AI-specific markup. Other providers differ; inclusion and citations are not guaranteed.

Source review date: 2026-11-12. Crawler-log verification date: 2026-11-14 (OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity provider guidance).

Suggested testing tools#

Choose tools appropriate to the project's stack and risks; automation supports evidence but does not approve the checklist.

  • Test focus: machine-readable answers, structured data, citation links, and content consistency (not rankings); include API and service behavior where applicable.
  • Cross-stack: Schema.org Validator + lychee.
  • Python: Beautiful Soup + pytest; for pytest-based suites, run python -m pytest -q.
  • TypeScript: Playwright + schema-dts + Vitest; for Vitest-based suites, run npx vitest run (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • JavaScript: Playwright + Ajv + Jest; for Jest-based suites, run npx jest --ci (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • Optional owned-site AI-fetch diagnostic: A case-insensitive log search for OAI-SearchBot|ChatGPT-User|Claude-SearchBot|Claude-User|PerplexityBot|Perplexity-User can identify candidate requests only. It mixes automated search crawlers with user-triggered fetchers, can match spoofed strings, misses unidentified traffic and says nothing by itself about citations. Where supported, cross-check provider-published IP lists/verified bot metadata and include edge-blocked requests, HTTP status codes, route grouping, time windows and log retention gaps. See GEO-081 and general privacy-safe logging under OBS-018/019.
  • Evidence: Save tool versions, configuration, test environment, fixtures, results, and links in project-specific review records using the existing checklist IDs. Expert review remains necessary where relevant.

Suggested AI skills for verification#

These are optional agent review aids, not automated passes or release approval. Each linked repository had at least 1,000 GitHub stars when checked on 2026-11-12; counts are per repository, not per skill, and do not indicate security or correctness.

  • ai-seo — Review answer-engine discoverability and source quality (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • schema — Check machine-readable content structure (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • seo-audit — Identify crawl and citation-link issues (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).

How to check: In a project-specific copy, have the agent audit the backend / API scope and map findings to this file's existing checklist IDs, with code/configuration references, reproducible test results, failed or inapplicable cases, and uncertainties. Independently verify findings; keep shared template boxes unchecked and retain human approval requirements.

Before use: Read the skill's SKILL.md, referenced scripts, license, and requested tool permissions. Only execute vetted skills with appropriate access in a controlled environment.

Important warning: reference only#

⚠️ Reference only — not a definitive or exhaustive checklist. This template is a starting point for review, not the ultimate authority or a guarantee of project safety, quality, regulatory compliance, accessibility, security, or launch readiness.

Use project-specific judgment and independent verification. Requirements and risks evolve and differ by project, technology, and jurisdiction. Adapt the checks, consult current authoritative sources, perform relevant tests, and obtain qualified specialist review or approval when appropriate. Checking every box does not replace these steps.

Reference, not a certification. Check applicability, verify important claims against current primary sources, and seek expert review where necessary. Suggest an improvement.
